title: Keep each wagon definition semantically coherent

facts.note: Primary and sufficient trigger: any identifiable wagon definition (complete or incomplete) is subject to this unconditional constraint.
Any authoring, editing or review of a wagon definition; no change-type exclusion.
Informational only, NOT a gate: a field-level diff helps focus which checks are touched, but the rule applies to the whole wagon definition regardless.
Supplementary signal only, NOT required: helps activate when a wagon is planned before its file exists.

fires: Planner writes a new wagon definition, even if some fields are still missing
Planner edits any part of an existing wagon definition, including formatting
Planner adds or moves a produce or consume artifact on a wagon
Planner reviews or validates an existing wagon definition
doesNotFire: Editing feature or code files that do not touch any wagon definition
Editing a theme or train document that contains no wagon definition

when: the planner creates, edits or validates that wagon definition
then: Make the wagon semantically coherent: the subject can perform the action, the action serves the goal, the outcome is a measurable result of the action, and the context makes sense for when/where the action occurs.
prefer: Phrase the outcome as a measurable result of the action
Declare as produce only artifacts this wagon owns, and mark at least one produce artifact scope: 'external'
Declare as consume only artifacts owned by other wagons
avoid: A subject that cannot perform the action, or an action that does not serve the goal
Outcomes that are not a measurable result of the action
Context that does not make sense for when/where the action occurs
Listing as produce an artifact not owned by this wagon
Consuming an artifact owned by this same wagon
A wagon with no produce artifact of scope: 'external'
why: A wagon must be semantically coherent: subject/action/goal align, outcome is measurable, produce is owned, consume is foreign, and at least one produce is external.
evidence: Each coherence_check passes on the wagon definition: subject↔action, action↔goal, outcome measurable from action, context makes sense for when/where action occurs
Every produce artifact is owned by this wagon; every consume artifact is owned by a different wagon
At least one produce artifact has scope: 'external'
verifier_detail: Seven coherence checks (source content.constraints): (1) subject and action align — subject can perform the action; (2) action and goal align — action serves the goal; (3) outcome is a measurable result of the action; (4) all produce artifacts owned by this wagon; (5) all consume artifacts owned by different wagons; (6) context makes sense for when/where the action occurs; (7) at least one produce artifact has scope: 'external'.
Checks 4, 5, 7 are mechanically decidable from artifact ownership/scope; checks 1–3 and 6 are llm_judged.
Term coherence_check: one semantic-coherence validation on a wagon definition.
audit: Source statement: A wagon must be semantically coherent: subject/action/goal align, outcome is measurable, produce is owned, consume is foreign, and at least one produce is external.

additions.text: Artifact ownership/scope checks (produce owned, consume foreign, ≥1 external produce) are an independent, mechanically checkable obligation; kept here in prefer/avoid/evidence/verifier_detail and proposed as planner.wagon.artifact-ownership-coherence.

additions.justification: Source has no activation section; required by schema, derived from the rule's subject (wagon definitions). The constraint is unconditional, so only the wagon-definition file_kind gates activation; change and task_term facts are non-gating signals.

trace.note: Summary statement used verbatim as why; components distributed to then/prefer/avoid.
